C01: Bacterial Infections and Mycoses: Infections caused by prokaryotic microorganisms including various bacteria and eukaryotic fungi. This category encompasses systemic and localized pathological processes such as bacteremia, septicemia, and toxemia. Bacterial pathogens involve Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms like Staphylococcus, Streptococcus, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It includes complex host-pathogen interactions, inflammatory responses, and tissue necrosis. Mycoses involve fungal agents such as yeasts and molds, leading to superficial, subcutaneous, or systemic infections like candidiasis and aspergillosis. Clinical hallmarks include fever, leukocytosis, suppuration, and specific antimicrobial resistance patterns. Focus on cellular wall structures, exotoxins, and endotoxins that trigger the innate immune system.
C02: Virus Diseases: Pathological conditions resulting from the invasion of host cells by viral agents containing either DNA or RNA genomes. This includes acute, chronic, and latent infections such as influenza, hepatitis, HIV/AIDS, and herpesvirus-related disorders. The category emphasizes viral replication cycles, attachment to cellular receptors, uncoating, and genomic integration. Pathogenesis involves cytopathic effects, oncogenic transformation, and evasion of the host interferon response. Key concepts include viral load, seroconversion, viral envelopes, and the mechanisms of antiviral drug resistance. It covers a broad spectrum from respiratory viremia to neurotropic viral syndromes affecting the central nervous system.
C03: Parasitic Diseases: Infections caused by protozoa, helminths (worms), and ectoparasites that live on or within a host organism. This category involves complex biological lifecycles, often requiring intermediate vectors like mosquitoes or snails. Major diseases include malaria (Plasmodium), schistosomiasis, and various intestinal infestations. Pathological mechanisms involve direct tissue damage, nutrient competition, and chronic immunopathological reactions such as granuloma formation. Keywords include trophozoites, oocysts, parasitic load, and zoonotic transmission. These conditions often present with peripheral eosinophilia and require specialized antiparasitic therapeutic interventions.
C04: Neoplasms: The study and clinical management of abnormal cellular proliferation, encompassing benign and malignant tumors. This category focuses on oncogenesis, the molecular biology of cancer cells, and the mechanisms of metastasis and tissue invasion. It includes various histological types such as carcinomas, sarcomas, lymphomas, and leukemias. Key concepts involve tumor staging (TNM system), grading, angiogenesis, apoptosis evasion, and the tumor microenvironment. Clinical diagnostic markers, biopsy findings, and paraneoplastic syndromes are central. Discussions often center on genomic instability, oncogene activation, and response to chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or immunotherapy.
C05: Musculoskeletal Diseases: Conditions affecting the skeletal system, joints, muscles, and associated connective tissues like ligaments and tendons. This includes degenerative diseases such as osteoarthritis, autoimmune disorders like rheumatoid arthritis, and metabolic bone diseases such as osteoporosis. Pathophysiology involves cartilage degradation, synovial inflammation, bone remodeling imbalances, and neuromuscular junction dysfunction. It covers traumatic injuries, congenital deformities, and myopathies. Key terminology includes arthropathy, osteoblast/osteoclast activity, muscle atrophy, and joint hypermobility. Clinical assessment often involves range of motion, inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP), and advanced musculoskeletal imaging.
C06: Digestive System Diseases: Disorders involving the gastrointestinal tract (esophagus, stomach, intestines) and accessory organs such as the liver, gallbladder, and pancreas. This category covers inflammatory bowel diseases (Crohn’s, ulcerative colitis), peptic ulcer disease, and hepatic conditions like cirrhosis and hepatitis. Pathogenesis involves motility disorders, malabsorption, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, and neoplastic changes. Key focus areas include acid-base balance, enzymatic digestion, gut microbiota, and portal hypertension. Clinical manifestations include dyspepsia, jaundice, occult blood, and changes in bowel habits. It integrates endoscopic findings, hepatic enzyme profiles, and metabolic dysfunction related to nutrient processing.
C07: Stomatognathic Diseases: Pathologies affecting the oral cavity, teeth, jaws, and associated structures like salivary glands and the temporomandibular joint. This includes dental caries, periodontitis, oral neoplasms, and maxillofacial deformities. Focus is on oral microbiology, dental pulp pathology, and the systemic impact of oral infections. Key concepts include plaque formation, gingival recession, malocclusion, and xerostomia. It covers both inflammatory conditions and structural abnormalities requiring dental or maxillofacial surgical intervention.
C08: Respiratory Tract Diseases: Conditions affecting the airways, lungs, and the mechanics of breathing. This category includes obstructive lung diseases (asthma, COPD), restrictive disorders (pulmonary fibrosis), and infectious processes like pneumonia and tuberculosis. Pathophysiology focuses on gas exchange efficiency, alveolar-capillary membrane integrity, and airway hyperresponsiveness. Key clinical markers include spirometry values (FEV1/FVC), blood gas analysis (hypoxia, hypercapnia), and pulmonary hypertension. It covers pleural diseases, such as pleurisy and effusion, and the impact of environmental pollutants on respiratory health.
C09: Otorhinolaryngologic Diseases: Disorders of the ear, nose, and throat (ENT) and related structures of the head and neck. This encompasses hearing loss, otitis media, vestibular disorders (vertigo), sinusitis, and laryngeal pathologies. Key focus areas include auditory perception, olfactory function, and upper airway obstruction. Terminology involves the tympanic membrane, Eustachian tube dysfunction, and nasal polyposis. It addresses both infectious and non-infectious etiologies, including allergic rhinitis and ENT-related neoplasms.
C10: Nervous System Diseases: Pathologies of the central nervous system (brain, spinal cord) and the peripheral nervous system. This category includes neurodegenerative diseases (Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s), demyelinating disorders (Multiple Sclerosis), cerebrovascular accidents (stroke), and epilepsy. Pathophysiology involves neuronal death, synaptic dysfunction, neurotransmitter imbalances, and blood-brain barrier disruption. Key clinical signs include motor deficits, sensory loss, cognitive decline, and abnormal electroencephalogram (EEG) patterns. It addresses intracranial pressure, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) abnormalities, and the complex etiology of neuropathic pain.
C11: Eye Diseases: Disorders affecting the visual system, including the eyeball, optic nerve, and extraocular structures. Major conditions include glaucoma, cataracts, macular degeneration, and diabetic retinopathy. Pathogenesis focuses on intraocular pressure, retinal vascularity, and lens clarity. Terminology includes visual acuity, refractive errors, uveitis, and corneal dystrophy. Clinical management involves ophthalmic surgery and the use of pharmacological agents to preserve vision or treat ocular surface diseases.
C12: Urologic and Male Genital Diseases: Conditions of the urinary tract in both genders and the reproductive system in males. This includes renal failure, urolithiasis (kidney stones), urinary tract infections, and prostatic disorders like BPH and prostate cancer. Pathophysiology focuses on glomerular filtration, tubular function, micturition mechanics, and hormonal regulation of male fertility. Key markers include creatinine clearance, proteinuria, and PSA levels. It addresses both obstructive uropathy and systemic complications of chronic kidney disease.
C13: Female Genital Diseases and Pregnan: Disorders of the female reproductive organs and complications related to the various stages of pregnancy, labor, and the puerperium. This includes endometriosis, polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), gynecological cancers, and obstetric issues such as pre-eclampsia and ectopic pregnancy. Focus is on hormonal cycles, placental function, and fetal-maternal health. Key terminology includes menstruation, gestation, pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), and neonatal outcomes related to maternal health.
C14: Cardiovascular Diseases: Disorders of the heart, blood vessels, and the systemic circulation. This category focuses on atherosclerosis, ischemic heart disease (myocardial infarction), heart failure, and cardiac arrhythmias. Pathophysiology involves hemodynamics, ventricular remodeling, valvular dysfunction, and vascular resistance. Key diagnostic markers include troponins, BNP, and electrocardiographic (ECG) changes. It covers hypertension, peripheral vascular disease, and the structural integrity of the myocardium and great vessels. The emphasis is on pump efficiency and the prevention of thrombotic events.
C15: Hemic and Lymphatic Diseases: Pathologies affecting the blood, bone marrow, and lymphatic system. This includes various anemias, coagulopathies (hemophilia, thrombosis), and malignancies such as leukemia and lymphoma. Pathophysiology involves hematopoiesis, red cell morphology, white cell function, and the lymphatic drainage system. Key concepts include hemoglobinopathy, splenomegaly, lymphadenopathy, and the role of clotting factors. It covers immune-mediated blood disorders and systemic manifestations of hematological failure.
C16: Neonatal Diseases and Abnormalities: Conditions originating in the prenatal period or during the first month of life, including congenital malformations and genetic syndromes. This category addresses prematurity, birth trauma, neonatal jaundice, and congenital heart defects. Focus is on developmental biology, teratogenesis, and neonatological intensive care. Key concepts include APGAR scores, chromosomal abnormalities, and metabolic screening for newborns.
C17: Skin and Connective Tissue Diseases: Dermatological disorders and systemic diseases affecting the skin and its underlying connective tissues. This includes inflammatory conditions (dermatitis, psoriasis), infections, and systemic sclerosis. Pathophysiology involves collagen synthesis, epidermal turnover, and autoimmune-mediated skin damage (Lupus). Terminology includes erythema, papules, pruritus, and the structure of the dermis. It addresses skin cancers, wound healing, and the cutaneous manifestations of systemic diseases.
C18: Nutritional and Metabolic Diseases: Disorders resulting from nutritional deficiencies, excesses, or imbalances in metabolic pathways. This category includes obesity, diabetes mellitus, malnutrition, and inborn errors of metabolism. Focus is on glucose homeostasis, lipid metabolism, electrolyte balance, and the role of vitamins and minerals. Pathogenesis involves insulin resistance, enzymatic defects, and metabolic syndrome. Clinical markers include HbA1c, cholesterol profiles, and body mass index (BMI).
C19: Endocrine Diseases: Pathologies of the ductless glands and the hormones they secrete. This includes disorders of the thyroid (hypo/hyperthyroidism), adrenal glands (Cushing’s, Addison’s), pituitary gland, and parathyroid. Pathophysiology focuses on feedback loops, hormone synthesis, and glandular hyperplasia or neoplasia. Key concepts include endocrine signaling, target organ response, and the systemic effects of hormonal dysregulation.
C20: Immunologic Diseases: Disorders caused by dysfunction of the immune system, encompassing hypersensitivity, autoimmunity, and immunodeficiency. This includes asthma, systemic lupus erythematosus, and primary or acquired immune failures. Pathogenesis involves T-cell and B-cell mediated responses, cytokine signaling, and antigen-antibody complexes. Key terminology includes anaphylaxis, tolerance, histocompatibility, and immunosuppression.
C21: Disorders of Environmental Origin: Conditions caused by external physical, chemical, or environmental factors. This includes injuries from radiation, thermal extremes (burns, frostbite), poisoning, and occupational hazards. Pathophysiology focuses on toxicity mechanisms, cellular damage from environmental stressors, and trauma. It covers air pollution effects, heavy metal poisoning, and the long-term impact of environmental exposures on human health.
C22: Animal Diseases: Pathological conditions occurring in non-human animals that have relevance to human medicine, either as zoonoses or as comparative models. This includes species-specific infections, animal models of human disease, and veterinary public health. Focus is on cross-species transmission, comparative anatomy, and the epidemiological links between animal and human health (One Health concept).
C23: Pathological Conditions, Signs and: Broad category for clinical manifestations, laboratory abnormalities, and general pathological findings that are not specific to a single organ system. This includes fever, pain, edema, fatigue, and non-specific inflammatory signs. It serves as a repository for diagnostic findings like abnormal imaging or laboratory markers (e.g., elevated CRP) and clinical signs observed during physical examination. Key focus is on the symptomatic presentation of disease and the classification of syndromes.
